newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai bourse suspends trading in two A shares.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai bourse suspends trading in two A shares.

text.p: The Shanghai stock exchange has suspended trading in two A share firms for alleged irregularities, traders said on Friday.
Prices of the A shares of Shenying Neu-Alpine Software Co and Hebei Weiyuan Industry Co were found to have moved abnomally and the exchanges had suspended their trading, they said.
An official with the Shanghai exchange said that the bourse had suspended trading in the two A share firms by order of the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC).
The CSRC found that prices in the two A shares had fluctuated abnormally and would investigate possible irregularities behind the trading, the official said.
Officials at the CSRC declined to comment.
Traders said the exchange had sent notices to the board of directors of the two firms, demanding that the five biggest holders of the firms's public shares report to the exchange.
No other details were immediately available.
Shanghai's A share index was down 5.85 percent and the B share index down 3.45 percent in early Friday afternoon trading after the exchange suspended trading in two A share firms, brokers said.
The Shanghai stock exchange later confirmed it had suspended trading because of abnormal fluctuations in their share prices, an exchange statement said.
"Share prices in the two A shares firms fluctuated in recent days and in line with securities rules the exchange suspended trading in the shares this afternoon," the statement said.
The exchange orders the firms and the five biggest holders of the two firms' public shares to give an explanation this afternoon, the statement said.

Spokesmen for the two firms said the price movements of their shares were a part of regular market activity and had nothing to do with the companies. They said they would make statements on the issue this afternoon.
